final_candidates.decision_summary: Q168Y (Q498Y in standard numbering) is in the ACE2-binding hotspot, has high ESM-1v plausibility, and the strongest evolutionary support among the top candidates. It likely improves receptor affinity while remaining structurally tolerated.

N171Y (N501Y) is the well-characterized ACE2-affinity-enhancing mutation despite low MSA frequency; the strong PLM score and low toxicity support viability. It is a canonical choice for improving RBD–ACE2 binding.

Y123F (Y453F) is a conservative aromatic substitution with high PLM plausibility and the lowest toxicity signal among retained candidates. It occurs in the ACE2-interface region and is consistent with receptor-binding adaptation.

stop_reason.detail: All four permitted tool calls have been consumed; no additional evidence is available to meaningfully revise the top three.

history.rationale: N501Y (N171Y in this numbering) is a well-characterized mutation that increases ACE2 binding affinity in multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Alpha and Omicron.
Moderate PLM but zero evolutionary support; downgraded from initial high confidence, though still active as an aromatic RBM substitution.

Moderate PLM (0.696) and some evolutionary support (0.333) but less competitive than higher-ranked candidates, so moved down.
